name: sore-throat-borderline
description: Borderline: introduces properly and reaches the pharmacy, but wavers under pushback by offering a GP booking, asks little, and gives a thin explanation.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hello, is that the surgery? I need an appointment with the doctor please.

transcript.speaker: trainee
transcript.text: Good morning, Pen-y-Bryn Surgery, Sam speaking. Who's calling please?

transcript.speaker: trainee
transcript.text: Thanks Carys. Is that for you?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes. I've had a sore throat for two days and I want antibiotics.

transcript.speaker: trainee
transcript.text: Okay. I think the pharmacy would be the best place for that.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Oh. But I need antibiotics, only the doctor can give those, can't I?

transcript.speaker: trainee
transcript.text: Well, I could book you in for Thursday if you'd rather, but the pharmacy would probably be quicker.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hm. Thursday's a bit far. Can they really give me antibiotics?

transcript.speaker: trainee
transcript.text: They can look at your throat and treat you if it's needed, yes.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Okay, I'll try the pharmacy then.

expect.flagsReason: She was sent to the pharmacy in the end but the receptionist offered a GP slot first; an honest reader could say outcomeCorrect either way, so it is not asserted.

greeting.reason: Own name and practice given, asked who was calling and whether it was for her.

information.reason: Asked about swallowing only; did not ask about breathing or conditions and medicines.

destination.reason: Ended at the pharmacy, but offered a GP booking as an option; 2 if the final destination is all that counts.

explanation.reason: Where and a thin why ("could treat you"); no advice on what to do if worse.

manner.reason: Polite, but wavered and ended abruptly.
